newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB falls on poor JGB auction, option-linked sale.
newsitem.headline: JGB falls on poor JGB auction, option-linked sale.

text.p: Key June JGB futures contract ended lower on Tuesday in response to poor results of the four-year JGB auction and option-linked selling, traders said.
June ended at 123.15, down from Monday's 123.66. It moved within a range of 122.81-123.69.
The auction for 500 billion yen worth of 1.7 percent four-year JGB notes resulted in a long-tail due to weak bids from underwriters.
It produced the lowest price of 98.91 or a stop rate of 1.994 percent and an average price of 99.05 or a yield of 1.955 percent.
The absence of Nomura Securities Co from the underwriting syndicate for the note was one factor behind the bad auction results, traders said.

The Ministry of Finance recently suspended Nomura from underwriting JGBs and government-guaranteed bonds until the implementation of administrative punishments against the firm, which is under investigation for allegedly making illegal payoffs to racketeers.
"Usually, other big-four brokerages make up for the absence (of Nomura) and place healthy bids at the auction, but that wasn't the case today," said a city bank trader.
The JGB market was bearish from early trade due to option-linked selling and weakness in less liquid debts such as government guaranteed and municipal bonds, traders said.
"A large-lot offer worth 700 contracts was seen this morning around 123.45 and this triggered the fall in JGBs. An additional 300 contracts were sold later on," a senior city bank trader said.

The heavy sales were believed to have come from U.S. hedge funds which are holding a large amount of June JGB put options with a strike price of 123.00. Open interest in the 123.00 June JGB futures put options totalled 12,564 contracts as of Monday.
About half of the open interest reflected long positions held by the hedge funds, said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
Traders said the hedge funds were selling June JGB futures this morning in an attempt to bring those put options in the money before they expire at the end of this week.
The June's slide was further accelerated by selling of futures by option dealers who were delta hedging short positions in the 123.00 June JGB puts, a bank trader said.
The option dealers are hedging against a further fall in June JGBs below the put options' strike price of 123.00.
Despite the market tumble on Tuesday, institutional investors were on the buy-side in the JGB market, traders said.
"JGBs are apparently benefitting from 'flight-to-quality' purchases by investors," said a trader at a European brokerage.

The liquidity of the non-JGB debt markets has declined due to the absence of Nomura Securities, the major market maker of those markets, sending investors into more liquid JGBs with minimum credit-risk, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.650 percent at 0714 GMT, up from 2.580 percent on Monday.
